title: Console essentialization: criteria for dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown MVP
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Narrow the Console feature surface for launch so teams get core observability (latency + errors + per-route cost) without overengineering card variants or full trace retention. This ticket captures the ‘essentialization’ decision criteria: which dashboard cards, tracing primitives, and cost-breakdown views are must-haves vs deferred. The goal is to protect the end-to-end rollout schedule while keeping a clear path to reintroduce deferred items in follow-ups.
scope_changes: Keep: per-route latency p50/p95/time-series (rolling 1h, 24h) as a single consolidated card
Keep: per-model and per-route token cost estimate (daily aggregate) with a conservative error margin
Keep: basic trace sampling links (sampled span preview + link to full trace in tracing UI) for errors above 1% rate
Defer: full distributed trace timeline explorer (expand/collapse spans) — replaced by sampled span preview and link to full external trace view
Defer: per-user cost attribution for the MVP — scoped for follow-up (Q2 cycle)
Defer: complex card permutations (role-based card sets, Advanced filters) — implement single canonical card per metric with saved view planned later
Remove: synthetic scenario playback & replay telemetry from initial surface
Introduce temporary fallback: compressed insight cards (compact mode) to reduce cardinality and render cost for low-budget environments
removed_scope: Full trace storage retention UI and retention policy controls
Real-time per-request waterfall visualization in the main dashboard
kept_scope: Consolidated latency card with selectable percentile and time range
Error-rate card with top-3 routes and a single-click drill to sampled traces
Daily cost trend card (tokens and infra allocation) with export CSV
Route-level alert toggle (on/off) that links to rollout policies
decisions: Adopt a 'one-card' pattern: one canonical visualization per metric type to reduce implementation permutations and QA cost
Set telemetry event budget for MVP: summarized aggregates only (no high-cardinality runtime facets). Reason: cost and frontend performance constraints on hosted environments
Trace strategy: sample on error-first basis (100% of error traces up to 1k/day, 1% of successful requests capped) and provide link-to-full-trace for enterprise Dedicated/private customers
Cost estimation approach: use tokenized server-side aggregates + inflation margin of 8% for unknowns in first 7 days post-launch
tradeoffs: User experience vs velocity: removing the full trace explorer reduces immediate troubleshooting power for SREs but accelerates delivery by ~3 sprints
Signal fidelity vs cost: limiting event cardinality may hide rare regressions; mitigated by sample-based anomaly alerts and an opt-in higher-fidelity plan for Dedicated customers
Frontend complexity vs maintainability: consolidating cards reduces permutations and long-term maintenance burden but may disappoint early power users who requested customization
acceptance_criteria: Latency card renders within 350ms on a 3G throttled connection for typical 24h time range payloads
Latency p95 calculation matches backend analytics within a 2% delta for sampled routes over 24h
Error-rate card identifies top-3 routes and surfaces a sampled trace link for each route; sampled traces open in the dedicated trace viewer and show span summary
Daily cost trend card shows aggregated token cost and infra cost with CSV export; exported CSV includes date, route, token_count_estimate, estimated_cost
Trace sampling budget enforcement: no more than 1k error traces retained per org per day (sampling logs show enforcement)
E2E QA signoff: product + design + two eng reviewers approve visual and perf acceptance criteria in PR (links in comments)
Rollout gating: feature flag present and rollout plan document is published to Confluence with rollback criteria
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only (Console team + SEs) for 1 week to validate sampling and cost deltas
Beta: opt-in for 10% of orgs by usage band (low/med/high) for 2 weeks; compare cost deltas against baseline
GA: staged rollout at 25% increments with monitoring of unit cost and error signal; rollback gate if +20% cost delta or missing >2% of error traces
Enterprise enablement: Dedicated/private customers get a 'high-fidelity' opt-in to increase trace retention and per-user cost attribution
risks: Undetected regressions due to aggressive aggregation — mitigated via a small diagnostic bucket that keeps higher fidelity for sampled heavy routes
Backend compute cost spike from naive aggregation queries — mitigated by pre-aggregating in analytics pipeline and limiting cardinality
Customer pushback on removed per-user cost features — mitigated by clear comms and a prioritized follow-up ticket backlog
